reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A reversible witness relation.** `ش ه د` B001 supplies presence with direct witnessing. The active/passive pairing makes one term present as observer and the other present as object, while later the persecutors are witnesses of their own action (85:7) and God witnesses every thing (85:9). I infer that roles can nest: an observer may itself become observed. The pair therefore reads as a chain of exposure rather than two permanently separate identities.

2. **From seeing to admissible testimony.** `ش ه د` B002 supplies testimony or decisive report grounded in knowledge. The packet moves from this oath to perpetrators watching (85:7), divine total witnessing (85:9), and a preserved recitation (85:21-22). I infer that presence becomes testimony when its content is retained and later disclosed. The ayah consequently anticipates an evidentiary process, not merely spectatorship.

3. **Sign and signified.** `ش ه د` B008 supplies a visible sign that testifies to a time, state, or quality. The adjacent sky, promised day, trench-fire, gardens, armies, and tablet can each operate as signs, but the reading remains anchored in the fixed شاهد/مشهود pair: one is the indicator and one the state indicated. I infer the directional arrow from visible mark to otherwise hidden condition. The pair can therefore be read as “testifying sign and testified reality” alongside personal witness readings.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: In 85:7 the persecutors become witnesses to their own deed, unexpectedly collapsing observer and implicated actor. In 85:9 God is witness over every knowable thing, placing that local self-witness inside complete testimony; in 85:22 the record is preserved. These later ayat turn the active/passive pair into a nested evidentiary chain and newly strengthen `ش ه د` B008: visible action is itself a sign that survives its moment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A reversible forensic relation.** Lexical evidence: `ش ه د` B001, “presence with witnessing,” and B002, “testifying from knowledge.” Structural cue and role: the same root appears in active and passive nominal forms here, then returns as `شهود` in 85:7, where the people present are witnesses to what they themselves do. Presence supplies direct knowledge; the active/passive pairing supplies the two poles of testimony. Abductive move: I infer that 85:7 instantiates the abstract pair and makes an actor capable of becoming evidence against his own act. Reading change: `شاهد ومشهود` is no longer merely two unspecified oath objects; it becomes a role relation that can reverse upon the perpetrators.

2. **The witnessed object as a material sign.** Lexical evidence: `ش ه د` B008, “witnessing sign.” Structural cue and role: the following trench (`خ د د` B002), fire (`ن و ر` B002), and overt conduct (`ف ع ل` B001) leave a visible configuration, while 85:8 states the exclusive grievance that organized it. These details assign the `مشهود` pole the role of an event that bears its own marks. Abductive move: I infer that the material scene can testify, not only a speaking person; the packet supplies the sign branch and the visible sequence. Reading change: “witnessed” expands into “made evidentially manifest,” preserving a non-personal reading alongside personal witnessing.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 85:7 was the decisive surprise because witness and doer become co-referential, making the active/passive pair reversible rather than static. 85:8 then supplies the exclusive motive, so the witnessed material scene acquires explanatory as well as visual evidence.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_focus_trace_hermetic.note: Hermetic Focus Trace not requested for this bundle. Rebuild with --include-focus-trace, or --require-focus-trace when reader JSON must be present.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
